D21·3zrg — 2026-09-16
rule: The boot stub interprets exactly one core exit code, 64, as "TypeScript runs it"; the core never reads stdin or writes a byte before returning 64, and a new dispatched shape or a second interpreted exit needs a Decision citing this one.
chose: The boot stub (cli/boot.ts, rust-core 3.1) dispatches by exit code, not by re-parsing argv: every `event`, `statusline` and `status` argv is spawned on the native core with stdio inherited and `SOFAR_CORE_DISPATCHED=1`; the core's exit 64 (NotOurs, or a styled `status`) means "run the TypeScript CLI on the same argv" — the core reads no stdin before deciding and prints no exit-64 diagnostic when dispatched, so the fallback sees whole stdin and clean streams — and every other exit is mirrored. The core is `SOFAR_CORE=<path>` (`0`/empty forbids one), else the platform package `@sofar/core-<platform>-<arch>` resolved from the stub (the one constant 3.2 may rename); absent means TypeScript silently, a named core that cannot spawn warns once and falls back, a signal-killed core exits 1 (stdin gone, no fallback). The update-refresh claim moves to the stub after a core-rendered `statusline`/`status` (cli/update-cache.ts, node builtins only, shared with update-check.ts), keeping the O2 ruling that the binary only reads the cache; `sofar-core status` renders the stderr notice with the stderr caps ladder. Proof: the reference conformance suite with `SOFAR_CORE=$PWD/target/release/sofar-core` — 27/27 cases, no tag skipped, `event append`, styled `status` and `commit-trailer` reaching TypeScript through the stub's own fallback — plus a fake-core dispatch test under `npm test` and a negative control (a core that always exits 1 fails 25/27). The hook shims keep `exec sofar event <hook>`: a direct exec needs a stable per-machine binary path, which is the 3.2 install layout's to settle.
over: The stub re-implementing the argv grammar (a third copy of parseRoot/dispatch) or the colour ladder to decide the styled-status case itself; capturing the core's stderr to hide the exit-64 diagnostics (changes the child's stderr TTY-ness, so a human at a terminal would get a plain notice where TypeScript colours it); the core claiming and spawning the refresh itself (O2, rejected); rewriting the shims to exec the binary now with an install path guessed ahead of 3.2.
because: Exit 64 is already the contract HOTPATH pins for "not mine" and D14 chose it precisely because the shim cannot know the colour ladder outcome; one env marker keeps both diagnostics for a human running sofar-core directly while the stub's fallback is the answer under dispatch. Sharing update-cache.ts between the stub and update-check.ts keeps one refresh policy, and the stub's cost is a file read only after a core-rendered statusline or status. The unfiltered run is the standalone 3.1 proof the plan asked for and is the shape the 3.3 gate and the 4.1 arm will use.
